title: Controllable charge-spin conversion in sliding multiferroic metal Fe3GaTe2
authors: Tongrui Li, Lidong Zhang, Weiyi Pan
abstract: Controlling charge--spin conversion within a single magnetic material is important for compact spintronic devices. Using first-principles calculations, symmetry analysis, and Wannier-based linear response, we study the Edelstein and spin Hall responses of sliding-ferroelectric bilayer \ce{Fe3GaTe2}. Two degenerate ground states with opposite interlayer sliding vectors and out-of-plane dipole moments are separated by a calculated switching barrier of about $16.3$~meV per unit cell. Magnetization orientation determines the allowed current-induced spin components, while ferroelectric switching induces component-selective sign reversals governed by $M_z\mathcal T$ for in-plane magnetization and by $M_z$ for out-of-plane magnetization. The Edelstein response is strongly energy dependent, with spin accumulation approaching $2~\hbar$ for $\mathbf m\parallel+y$ under a reference field of $1$~V/Å. Momentum-resolved analysis links the TR-even and TR-odd Edelstein responses to $Γ$-centered constant-energy contours and localized interband features, respectively. Spin-conductivity contributions show the opposite momentum-space character, with broad sign-competing spin Berry curvature for TR-even and narrow Fermi-surface contours for TR-odd. The transverse spin Hall conductivity reaches $\sim10^{3}\,(\hbar/e)(\mathrm{S/cm})$ and depends strongly on ferroelectric state and magnetization direction. Magnetization rotations in the $xy$ and $xz$ planes reveal symmetry-allowed higher angular harmonics in both spin accumulation and spin-current responses. These results establish sliding-ferroelectric bilayer \ce{Fe3GaTe2} as a tunable platform for reconfigurable spin accumulation and spin-current generation.
summary: This theoretical study demonstrates that the bilayer Fe3GaTe2 can function as a highly tunable platform for charge-spin conversion. By combining ferroelectric switching and magnetic field control, researchers can selectively manipulate the spin accumulation and spin-current generation. This work highlights the potential of multiferroic metals for next-generation spintronic devices.
main_problem: The study investigates how charge-spin conversion can be controllably manipulated within a single magnetic material by exploiting the interplay between ferroelectricity and magnetism.
main_result: The sliding-ferroelectric bilayer Fe3GaTe2 is established as a tunable platform where both the ferroelectric state and the magnetization direction can selectively control the magnitude and sign of the spin accumulation and spin-current responses.
method: The research employs first-principles calculations, symmetry analysis, and Wannier-based linear response theory to model the Edelstein and spin Hall responses.
model_or_system: The physical system is the sliding-ferroelectric bilayer Fe3GaTe2. The analysis uses a tight-binding Hamiltonian derived from Fe-d, Ga-p, and Te-p orbitals, incorporating spin-orbit coupling and considering two degenerate ferroelectric ground states.
key_observables: Edelstein response ($\delta S_i$), transverse spin Hall conductivity ($\sigma_{SH}$), spin accumulation ($\delta \mathbf{S}_i$), and spin-current responses ($\mathbf{J}_{\alpha i}$).
important_parameters: The switching barrier ($\approx 16.3 	ext{ meV}$), the electric field strength ($1 	ext{ V}/	ext{\AA}$ or $10^{10} 	ext{ V/m}$), and the broadening parameter ($\Gamma = 10 	ext{ meV}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis separates responses into TR-even and TR-odd components based on magnetization reversal, and the linear response formalism is used.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate layer-resolved current-induced spin accumulation ($\delta S$) and spin conductivity ($\sigma$) components for different magnetization directions and polarization states.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the dependence of charge-spin conversion on the ferroelectric state and magnetization direction, detailing the energy dependence of the Edelstein response and the momentum-space character of the spin conductivity.
why_interesting: The ability to use electric fields (ferroelectricity) to tune spin-charge conversion in a magnetic material is a key concept in spintronics, which is highly relevant to understanding emergent phenomena in strongly correlated and functional electronic materials.
